title: Deferred ActorInstantiate path submits a Lua require request

Q1_lazy_on_resolve.verdict: NO. Resolve uses FUN_00CD8870(name, create=0) - it does not load. Class definition is eager-via-Lua-require, not lazy-on-resolve.

Q2_what_triggers_the_load.verdict: Lua require reaches FUN_00D08A10 -> FUN_00D0CFB0 -> FUN_00D08180 -> FUN_00CF4680 and executes a supplied chunk. Deferred ActorInstantiate also supplies a native trigger: FUN_007663D0 retains the descriptor, adds +0xAC at VA 0x0076678A and calls FUN_00CC76F0 at VA 0x00766794. FUN_00CD7DA0 -> FUN_00D0C440 queues that path and listener. FUN_00D0C070 supplies require, path, listener and byte argument at VA 0x00D0C1FF..0x00D0C259. A data-only xref to the Lua C function does not exclude this queued native submission. Class definition and successful completion remain separate from submission.

Q3_player_vs_director.verdict: The core preload list includes Player and WorldMaster paths. Deferred network records can submit their received script paths through the same engine require queue. These static inputs do not establish any particular content class load outcome or explain a failed runtime binding.

Q4_what_server_must_send.verdict: The deferred route consumes the received class and script path independently. The supplied module must define the selected class and preserve its base dependencies; class-dependent creation still requires a valid class. The client does not choose the module by numeric zone. Successful load, listener callback and first binding require their own evidence.
Q4_what_server_must_send.differentiator: ActorInstantiate application +0x24 supplies the class; the first tagged string at application +0x44 supplies the path. The deferred descriptor keeps that path at +0xAC and actively submits it. No opening-session outcome is inferred from this static join.

directorsArePureLua: Content classes are defined by supplied Lua chunks. The native _createActor operation requires an already defined class; deferred ActorInstantiate additionally submits its received module path before its later binding callback. Neither route guarantees a particular content initialization succeeds.
